lead.t: Hepatorenal syndrome (HRS) is a functional, rapidly progressive renal failure that occurs in patients with advanced chronic liver disease (usually cirrhosis) or acute severe liver injury, in the absence of intrinsic kidney pathology.

b: Renal failure in severe liver disease WITHOUT intrinsic kidney disease - Excluded: concomitant liver + kidney damage, ATN secondary to circulatory collapse - Pathogenesis: vasoconstriction → decreased renal blood flow - Urine : hyperosmolar

snip.t: | Hepatic failure with hepatorenal syndrome | Cirrhosis, ascites, low urine sodium | Usually responds to vasoconstrictor therapy; dialysis reserved for severe metabolic derangements |
| Hepatorenal syndrome – type 1 | Rapid creatinine rise, advanced cirrhosis, precipitating infection | No intrinsic renal pathology, FeNa <1 %, no casts |
Signs of chronic liver disease (spider naevi, palmar erythema): May coexist with hepatorenal syndrome in advanced disease.
